# Lumail.io

> The AI-native email platform for newsletters, automations, and transactional email.

Lumail lets teams and AI agents create campaigns, manage subscribers, automate email workflows, send transactional messages, and inspect delivery analytics from one organization-scoped platform. The browser application includes a visual email editor, capture pages, sending-domain setup, campaign scheduling, workflow automation, and deliverability controls. The same product surface is available to software and agents through OAuth, a hosted Model Context Protocol server, a REST API, a TypeScript SDK, and the Lumail CLI.

## Agent access

- MCP server: Streamable HTTP endpoint protected by OAuth 2.1 or organization API tokens.
- MCP server manifest: machine-readable transport, OAuth, documentation, and OpenAPI discovery.
- MCP install guide: machine-readable client setup instructions.
- OpenAPI 3.1 specification: typed REST operations and JSON error schemas.
- Agent documentation index: concise markdown index of every agent and developer resource.
- Full markdown documentation: concatenated public documentation for offline retrieval.

## Developer access

- REST API reference: subscriber, tag, event, campaign, and transactional-email operations.
- Authentication: organization-scoped bearer tokens and permissions.
- TypeScript SDK: typed application integration.
- CLI: install and operate Lumail from a terminal.
- MCP reference: transports, authentication, tools, resources, and limits.

## Product and support

- Pricing
- Documentation
- Support
- Sitemap

Questions about pricing
Do you charge per subscriber?
+
No. There is no subscriber limit on any plan, and no line on your invoice for list size. Import 50,000 contacts on day one if you want. The price only moves when you send.
So what will it actually cost me?
+
The first 3,000 emails each month are free, no card required. Creator is $20/month with 40,000 emails included. A 20,000-contact list emailed four times a month is 80,000 emails, costing $48. Use the calculator for your volume.
How is this different from Mailchimp, Kit, or Beehiiv?
+
Some competitors now expose MCP too, so compare the real workflow instead of the AI label. Lumail's full catalog has 126 organization-scoped tools across campaigns, workflows, subscribers, analytics, and transactional email, with a visual app, CLI, SDK, and API beside them. The billing model is the other difference: Lumail prices emails delivered and stores unlimited subscribers, so a dormant record does not raise your bill.
Can Lumail send my app's transactional emails too?
+
Yes, and that's the point. Point your app at our SMTP relay (smtp.lumail.io:587, STARTTLS) or the API and your password resets, receipts, and OTPs ship from the same place as your newsletter. They travel in a separate instant lane, so a 50,000-recipient campaign can never make a login code wait.
Do I need to be a developer to use Lumail?
+
No. Everything runs from the dashboard: a visual workflow builder, a filter builder for segments, and an AI-assisted editor. The API and SDK are there when you want them, not a prerequisite.
Can my AI agent run my newsletter?
+
If you already work in Claude Code, Cursor, or another MCP client, add your API token and 126 organization-aware tools show up. Ask for a campaign, a segment, or last month's numbers and the agent does it. Entirely optional. The dashboard does the same job.

Questions about pricing
Do you charge per subscriber?
+
No. There is no subscriber limit on any plan, and no line on your invoice for list size. Import 50,000 contacts on day one if you want. The price only moves when you send.
So what will it actually cost me?
+
The first 3,000 emails each month are free, no card required. Creator is $20/month with 40,000 emails included. A 20,000-contact list emailed four times a month is 80,000 emails, costing $48. Use the calculator for your volume.
How is this different from Mailchimp, Kit, or Beehiiv?
+
Some competitors now expose MCP too, so compare the real workflow instead of the AI label. Lumail's full catalog has 126 organization-scoped tools across campaigns, workflows, subscribers, analytics, and transactional email, with a visual app, CLI, SDK, and API beside them. The billing model is the other difference: Lumail prices emails delivered and stores unlimited subscribers, so a dormant record does not raise your bill.
Can Lumail send my app's transactional emails too?
+
Yes, and that's the point. Point your app at our SMTP relay (smtp.lumail.io:587, STARTTLS) or the API and your password resets, receipts, and OTPs ship from the same place as your newsletter. They travel in a separate instant lane, so a 50,000-recipient campaign can never make a login code wait.
Do I need to be a developer to use Lumail?
+
No. Everything runs from the dashboard: a visual workflow builder, a filter builder for segments, and an AI-assisted editor. The API and SDK are there when you want them, not a prerequisite.
Can my AI agent run my newsletter?
+
If you already work in Claude Code, Cursor, or another MCP client, add your API token and 126 organization-aware tools show up. Ask for a campaign, a segment, or last month's numbers and the agent does it. Entirely optional. The dashboard does the same job.

Synthesis:
Lumail.io provides an email marketing platform that integrates with AI agents via the Model Context Protocol to manage subscribers, campaigns, and graph-based workflows [1][2]. It offers two primary MCP connection paths: an OAuth endpoint at https://lumail.io/mcp for ChatGPT and Codex, which supports read and draft-write operations [3][4], and an SSE endpoint at https://lumail.io/api/mcp/sse for trusted clients like Claude and Cursor, which provides the full tool catalog and supports high-impact actions like sending or scheduling via confirmation gates [2][5]. The platform bills based on email volume rather than subscriber count [1][6].

<content>Connect Lumail to Codex and it can read your subscribers, campaigns, workflows and analytics, and draft new ones from the session where you write code. Authentication is a browser sign-in: `config.toml` holds a URL and nothing else.
...
Your agent fetches the machine-readable guide at lumail.io/codex/install, writes the config block, and tells you when to approve the browser prompt.
...
```toml
[mcp_servers.lumail]
url = "https://lumail.io/mcp"
oauth_resource = "https://lumail.io/mcp"

```
...
`lumail` should appear at `https://lumail.io/mcp`, connected. Inside the Codex TUI, `/mcp` shows the same. Start a new session before your first Lumail prompt so the tool list is picked up.
...
`https://lumail.io/mcp` is an OAuth 2.1 protected resource with dynamic client registration. Codex registers itself, runs PKCE, and stores the access token in its own credential store — so committing your dotfiles leaks nothing.
...
## What the connection can do

| Scope | Access |
| --- | --- |
| `lumail.read` | Subscribers, tags, custom fields, campaigns and their analytics, send progress, workflows, org stats, senders, snippets, writing style |
| `lumail.write` | Add subscribers, apply and remove tags in bulk, create and edit campaign drafts, duplicate campaigns, create and configure workflow drafts, enroll subscribers in a workflow |
...
Sending, scheduling, publishing or activating a workflow, unsubscribing, and every delete are not registered on the OAuth endpoint. They are not permission prompts an agent could talk you into — the tools simply do not exist on this connection.

Do that work in the Lumail app, or from your terminal with the CLI, which reaches the full API and signs in with the same browser flow:
...
OAuth settings are not discovered: the server URL must be exactly `https://lumail.io/mcp`, without `/api` or `/sse`.
...
"Needs authentication": re-run `codex mcp login lumail`, and check that no `bearer_token_env_var` line remains in the block.</content>

content.text: Deps installed. Now I'll inline the brand SVG paths into a TS module (avoids async image loading during render).

args.command:
mkdir -p src public && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,json
brands=[('Mailchimp','#FFE01B','#111111','mailchimp'),('Kit','#111111','#F7F8F8','kit'),('Brevo','#0B996E','#F7F8F8','brevo'),('Systeme.io','#00A0FF','#F7F8F8','systeme'),('beehiiv','#111111','#F7F8F8','beehiiv'),('ActiveCampaign','#356AE6','#F7F8F8','activecampaign'),('MailerLite','#09C269','#F7F8F8','mailerlite'),('Resend','#111111','#F7F8F8','resend')]
out=[]
for name,bg,fg,f in brands:
    s=open(f'../research/brands/{f}.svg').read()
    vb=re.search(r'viewBox="([^"]+)"',s).group(1)
    inner=re.sub(r'^[\s\S]*?<svg[^>]*>','',s)
    inner=re.sub(r'</svg>\s*$','',inner)
    inner=re.sub(r'<title>[\s\S]*?</title>','',inner).strip()
    out.append(dict(name=name,bg=bg,fg=fg,viewBox=vb,svg=inner))
    print(name, vb, len(inner), inner[:120])
open('src/brands.json','w').write(json.dumps(out,indent=1))
EOF

content.text:
The video and player are finished and checked: `video.mp4` is exactly 45 seconds at 1920×1080 (16:9), and it plays in `index.html` at every viewport size I tried.

**Files in the working directory**
- `video.mp4`: H.264 High at 60fps (2,700 frames), AAC stereo audio at 48kHz, 13.5 MB. The file is set up to start playing before it fully downloads, and the brand colors survived encoding (orange `#fd3200` against the brand's `#ff3300`, paper `#f7f7f3` against `#f8f7f4`).
- `index.html`: just a `<video controls playsinline>` element. The browser title is "Claude Opus 5.5", and there's no heading or other text on the page. The video is sized to the largest 16:9 box that fits the viewport:

```css
width:  min(100vw, 100dvh * 16 / 9);
height: min(100dvh, 100vw * 9 / 16);
```

There's also a `vh` fallback for older browsers, and the page is centered on a dark background.

**Playback check**
I ran headless Chrome through `motion/scripts/verify-player.mjs`, serving the folder from inside the script so no server was left running. At each size it checked the title, controls, video resolution, duration and that the video stays 16:9 and fits the screen. It also played the video, confirmed the time was advancing with no errors, then seeked to 42.5 seconds and took a screenshot.

| Viewport | Video size on page | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1920×1080 | 1920×1080 | fills the screen |
| 1280×1000 | 1280×720 | bars top and bottom |
| 1700×600 | 1067×600 | bars left and right |
| 390×844 | 390×219 | phone portrait, bars top and bottom |

All four passed: about 2.4 seconds of playback in 2.5 seconds, duration 45.000s. The screenshots are in `motion/stills/player-*.png`.

**Video content (Lumail's look: paper background, `#ff3300` orange, Geist type, hatched page rails)**
1. The logo tile pops in, the L draws itself and the "Lumail" wordmark forms, then the camera zooms through the tile into orange.
2. "Email marketing shouldn't feel like a second job": clutter cards blow away, then a curtain lifts.
3. The hero headline, with a domain being typed and "Start free" clicked, then the page scrolls on.
4. The AI agent: a terminal runs 126 tools, shows MCP tool calls, and a "Schedule" approval gets clicked. A fast whip-pan leads out.
5. The editor: an AI "Tighten" rewrite, then the editor card morphs into a workflow node.
6. The workflow builder goes live, and 14 contact avatars flow through the branches.
7. A dark transactional-email scene ("Replace Resend") with a priority lane for one-time codes, then a blinds transition.
8. Pricing: pay per email sent, unlimited subscribers stored, with a slider and plan cards.
9. "Migrate from [Mailchimp, Kit, Brevo and others] in less than 10 minutes", then the logo lockup, tagline, "Start free" button and lumail.io.

The soundtrack is generated in code and synced to the cuts: 120 BPM in A minor with whooshes, impacts and ticks, at −13.8 LUFS with a −1 dBFS peak.

**Rebuilding:** in `motion/`, run `pnpm render`, then `node scripts/soundtrack.mjs`, then the ffmpeg mux command. That command must keep `in_color_matrix=bt601`, because Remotion outputs BT.601 full-range video and without that flag the orange shifts to about `#ff4300`.

Your Mac is very slow right now because of old headless Chromium processes from other Playwright and dev-browser sessions. One has used about 900 minutes of CPU (PID 54624, and PID 2455 is similar). They aren't from this task, so I left them alone. `pkill -f chrome-headless-shell` would clear them if you don't need them.Those three were the checks from my last message. They only looked hung because the machine is heavily loaded, and all of them finished:

- **ffprobe** confirmed the final `video.mp4`: 45.000s, 1920×1080, 16:9, H.264 High at 60fps (2,700 frames), plus AAC stereo audio at 48kHz.
- **The process check** found stray headless Chromium processes left over from other Playwright and dev-browser sessions, not from this task. I didn't kill them.
- **The shell check** responded after about 23 seconds, so the shell was just slow.

Nothing more to do; `video.mp4` and `index.html` are finished and verified.
